trajectory_summary: The call opens cleanly and cooperatively, but the rep DQs the lead on a shading assumption pulled from a satellite map without probing further, and then does not update that read even after the customer twice offers specific corrective detail. The call ends with a vague, unanchored callback promise rather than a resolved outcome in either direction.

observed_outcome.quote: I don't think that the panels will be able to get enough sun, for them to be super fully fully beneficial to you.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep disqualifies the lead on shading grounds mid-call and closes with a vague, undated callback contingent on internal design-team review rather than a confirmed appointment — no day/time was ever set, so the practical outcome is a soft DQ, not a booking.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The call was cut short by the shading DQ before the rep ever reached the bill-amount question in the verify flow; no dollar figure or usage number was raised by either party.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The call ended at the shading/DQ stage, well before bill collection would normally occur in the script sequence.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked what interested the customer in solar; the call moved directly from address/tenure confirmation into the tree/shading assessment and DQ discussion.

I've got your address here as 1909 McFadden Street in Columbia, South Carolina. Is that correct?
script_coverage.customer_quote: We've only been renting it for about a little over a year, but, we've owned the home for a long time.

script_coverage.quote: So So I see that you have some trees around you. Are all of those trees still there?
script_coverage.customer_quote: But the trees really only only give shade on the portion of the house and only a part of the day, if that makes a difference.

script_coverage.quote: I can reach out to my design team and see if they would be able to do anything. And then if they can, I'll give you a callback, and we could totally get you scheduled. Okay?

objections.quote: Once I only have that side gets a lot. ... only give shade on the portion of the house and only a part of the day, if that makes a difference.
objections.reasoning: Customer pushes back on the shading DQ with specific corrective detail; the rep does not engage with a follow-up question and instead repeats the original conclusion at 02:20, so the customer's correction was never actually addressed.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Re-engaging after a customer correction to a DQ
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Once I once I have that side gets a lot. ... only give shade on the portion of the house and only a part of the day, if that makes a difference.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer handed the rep specific, usable detail that could have changed the shading assessment, and the rep repeated the same conclusion two lines later without a single follow-up question — this is the single most consequential and correctable gap on the call.

key_moments.quote: So I think that with those trees still there, I don't think that the panels will be able to get enough sun, for them to be super fully fully beneficial to you.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep reaches a hard-DQ-style conclusion from a satellite image alone without asking which side of the roof the trees shade or for what portion of the day — a process gap in how shading DQs should be verified before being delivered to the customer.

key_moments.quote: So, yeah, I really do apologize, but I can get you off our list if you don't get any more calls. Okay?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep moves straight from a tentative shading impression ('I think... I don't think') to offering to remove the customer from the list entirely — a disproportionate action given the DQ hasn't actually been verified.

key_moments.quote: Once I once I have that side gets a lot. ... only give shade on the portion of the house and only a part of the day, if that makes a difference.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer directly volunteers the exact information (which side gets sun, limited/partial shading) that would let the rep re-evaluate the DQ, and the rep does not ask a single follow-up question about it before repeating the same conclusion at 02:20.

key_moments.quote: I can reach out to my design team and see if they would be able to do anything. And then if they can, I'll give you a callback, and we could totally get you scheduled. Okay?
key_moments.stewart_read: The call ends with a conditional, undated callback promise instead of either a resolved DQ or a locked next step — no timeframe, no specific commitment, and no confirmation the customer even wants to be recontacted given the earlier list-removal offer.
